name: Question 4
problem:
Consider the set $A,$ defined as

$$
A={\frac{k}{5}:k\in Z}.
$$

Which of the following sets is equivalent to $A?$
worked_solution:
The elements of $A$ are all the terms of the sequence ${a}_{k},$ given by

$$
{a}_{k}=\frac{k}{5},\,k\in Z={0,\pm 1,\pm 2,\pm 3,…}.
$$

Let's write down some terms of our sequence until the pattern becomes clear.

$$
\begin{aligned} & ⋮ \\ {a}_{-3} & =\frac{(-3)}{5}=-\frac{3}{5} \\ {a}_{-2} & =\frac{(-2)}{5}=-\frac{2}{5} \\ {a}_{-1} & =\frac{(-1)}{5}=-\frac{1}{5} \\ {a}_{0} & =\frac{0}{5}=0 \\ {a}_{1} & =\frac{1}{5} \\ {a}_{2} & =\frac{2}{5} \\ {a}_{3} & =\frac{3}{5} \\  & ⋮\end{aligned}
$$

So, the set consists of the elements

$$
A={0,\pm \frac{1}{5},\pm \frac{2}{5},\pm \frac{3}{5},…}.
$$

Question 4
?

Consider the set A, defined as A={k5:k∈Z}. Which of the following sets is equivalent to A?

a
{±15,±25,±35,…}
b
{0,15,25,35,…}
c
{0,±15,±25,±35}
d
{0,±15,±25,±35,…}
e
{15,25,35,…}
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

The elements of A are all the terms of the sequence ak, given by ak=k5,k∈Z={0,±1,±2,±3,…}.

Let's write down some terms of our sequence until the pattern becomes clear. ⋮a−3=(−3)5=−35a−2=(−2)5=−25a−1=(−1)5=−15a0=05=0a1=15a2=25a3=35⋮

So, the set consists of the elements A={0,±15,±25,±35,…}.
